Regards,
Bellweather Croft LLP

edits.text: 1. Purchase Price; Adjustment. The aggregate purchase price for the Shares shall be USD 45,000,000 (the “Purchase Price”), subject to adjustment dollar-for-dollar for the amount by which Closing Working Capital is greater or less than the agreed Target Working Capital, and to the other adjustments expressly set forth in this Agreement. The parties shall agree before signing on the applicable accounting principles, illustrative calculation, and dispute-resolution procedure. The Purchase Price shall be reduced by Company indebtedness outstanding at Closing and increased by Company cash at Closing, in each case as defined and calculated under the agreed funds-flow and accounting procedures, without duplication. The Seller shall not cause any prohibited leakage between signing and Closing, other than expressly permitted leakage identified in this Agreement. The parties shall negotiate the definitions, permitted leakage, calculation mechanics, and any escrow or holdback in good faith.
edits.name: none

edits.text: 2. Closing. Closing shall occur within 30 days after signing, or on such other date as the parties agree in writing, subject to (a) satisfaction or waiver, to the extent legally permissible, of the conditions to Closing set forth in this Agreement and (b) completion of the Buyer’s due diligence. The parties shall cooperate in good faith to pursue diligence and satisfaction of the conditions promptly. The Closing date shall be extended as reasonably necessary to permit satisfaction or waiver of those conditions, subject to any applicable termination right.
edits.name: none

edits.text: 3. Seller Representations and Warranties. The Seller represents and warrants, as of signing and as of Closing (except for representations expressly made as of a specified date), that: (a) the Seller is duly organized, validly existing, and has power and authority to enter into and perform this Agreement; (b) execution and performance have been duly authorized and do not violate the Seller’s organizational documents or any material agreement or law applicable to the Seller; (c) the Shares constitute all of the issued and outstanding equity interests of the Company, are duly authorized, validly issued, fully paid and nonassessable, and the Seller has good title to them, free of liens other than permitted liens; (d) the financial statements delivered to Buyer were prepared in accordance with the accounting principles specified in this Agreement and fairly present, in all material respects, the Company’s financial position and results for the periods covered; (e) except as reflected, reserved against, or disclosed in the financial statements or disclosure schedules, the Company has no material liabilities required to be reflected under those accounting principles; (f) the Company has filed all material tax returns required to be filed and paid all material taxes due, subject to applicable extensions and good-faith contests disclosed to Buyer; (g) the Company is not in material breach of any material contract, and, to Seller’s knowledge, no counterparty is in material breach thereof; (h) there is no pending litigation against the Company that would reasonably be expected to be material to the Company, and, to Seller’s knowledge, none has been threatened in writing; (i) the Company is in material compliance with applicable employment laws with respect to its employees, and all material compensation obligations due have been paid or accrued; (j) the Company is in compliance in all material respects with laws applicable to its operation; and (k) no broker or finder is entitled to a fee from Buyer or the Company as a result of arrangements made by Seller. The representations shall be qualified by matters fairly disclosed in the disclosure schedules and by agreed materiality and knowledge qualifiers. The parties shall agree the form and scope of disclosure schedules before execution.
edits.name: none

edits.text: 4. Confidentiality. The terms of this Agreement and all non-public information exchanged in connection with the transaction shall be kept confidential, subject to customary exceptions for disclosures to a party’s representatives who are bound by confidentiality obligations, as required by law or regulation, or with the other party’s written consent. Any disclosure required by law shall, to the extent legally permitted, be preceded by reasonable notice and consultation.
edits.name: none

edits.text: 5. Covenants. From signing until Closing, Seller shall cause the Company to operate in the ordinary course consistent with past practice, subject to agreed exceptions and Buyer’s consent (not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed) for specified extraordinary actions. Seller shall use reasonable efforts to preserve the business and maintain material relationships. Buyer shall maintain confidentiality, provide reasonable cooperation, and promptly pursue its diligence and required approvals. Each party shall give prompt notice of material developments affecting its ability to close. Seller shall provide reasonable access to relevant books, records, personnel, and facilities during normal business hours, on reasonable advance notice, subject to applicable law, privilege, third-party restrictions, and reasonable measures to avoid undue disruption. No access or diligence investigation shall modify the express representations and warranties in this Agreement.
edits.name: none

edits.text: 6. Conditions to Closing. Buyer’s obligation to close shall be subject to (a) the Seller’s representations and warranties being true and correct at Closing, subject to agreed bring-down standards and materiality qualifiers; (b) Seller’s material performance of its covenants; (c) no injunction or law prohibiting the transaction; (d) receipt of agreed regulatory and third-party consents; and (e) completion of due diligence to Buyer’s satisfaction, acting reasonably and in good faith. Seller’s obligation to close shall be subject to Buyer’s representations being true and correct, Buyer’s material performance of its covenants, receipt of required approvals, and no injunction or law prohibiting the transaction. Conditions may be waived only in writing by the party entitled to their benefit, to the extent legally permissible.
edits.name: none

edits.text: 7. Termination. This Agreement may be terminated before Closing by mutual written consent; by either party if Closing has not occurred by the date 60 days after signing (the “Outside Date”), provided the terminating party is not then in material breach and the failure to close is not primarily attributable to its breach; by either party following a final, non-appealable order prohibiting the transaction; or by a party for the other party’s material breach, if the breach is not cured within 20 days after written notice (or is incapable of cure). Buyer may also terminate if its due diligence is not completed to its reasonable satisfaction by the Outside Date. Termination shall not affect accrued rights or provisions expressly surviving termination, including confidentiality and liability for pre-termination breach.
edits.name: none

edits.text: 8. Indemnification. Subject to definitive documentation and the limitations below, Seller shall indemnify Buyer for direct losses arising from breach of Seller’s representations, warranties, or covenants. Claims for general representations shall survive for 18 months after Closing; claims for fundamental representations (organization, authority, capitalization, and title to Shares) and tax matters shall survive for the applicable limitation period, subject to an agreed outside limit. No claim may be brought unless covered losses exceed an agreed basket, with recovery from the first dollar once an agreed deductible basket is exceeded. Seller’s aggregate liability for general representation claims shall be capped at an agreed percentage of the Purchase Price; fundamental representation and tax claims shall be subject to a separate, higher cap, not exceeding the Purchase Price, except as otherwise agreed. Covenants shall survive for the period stated in them or, if none, 18 months. No party shall recover duplicative damages or consequential, punitive, special, or exemplary damages, except to the extent actually awarded to a third party. Indemnification shall be the exclusive remedy after Closing, except for fraud, intentional misconduct, or equitable relief. Nothing herein limits liability for fraud; the parties shall agree the applicable standard and attribution.
edits.name: none

receiver.requested_changes:
Please revise the Purchase Price to USD 30,000,000, subject only to clearly defined, objectively calculated closing adjustments. The current draft leaves the target working capital, accounting principles, indebtedness and cash definitions, leakage rules, dispute procedure, and any escrow or holdback unresolved. Please provide proposed definitions, a sample funds flow and closing statement, and an illustrative working-capital calculation. The adjustment should prevent double counting, exclude items already reflected in working capital, and include a prompt post-closing statement and independent-accountant dispute process. Any escrow or holdback should be specified and should secure identified contingent liabilities or indemnification obligations, not be left for later negotiation.

Please provide a complete draft with customary, appropriately scoped representations and warranties covering, among other matters, the Company’s organization and authority, capitalization and title, financial statements and liabilities, taxes, material contracts, litigation, employees and benefits, compliance with law, permits, intellectual property, data privacy and security, environmental matters, insurance, and brokers. Please include disclosure schedules with the next draft. We propose a 24-month survival period for general representations, survival for fundamental and tax claims through the applicable limitation period, a meaningful general cap and a separate cap for fundamental and tax claims, and a materiality scrape for determining losses, subject to negotiated exceptions. Fraud should remain uncapped, with attribution limited to actual fraud by the person committing it. Please also specify the basket and deductible rather than leaving them open.

The 30-day closing provision should not require Buyer to close before satisfactory completion of diligence or satisfaction or waiver of closing conditions. Please include customary conditions, including accuracy of representations at closing, performance of covenants, delivery of required consents and closing deliverables, and no injunction. Buyer should have a termination right if diligence is unsatisfactory or conditions are not satisfied by an agreed outside date, without a penalty. Please provide the requested diligence materials through a secure data room, including financial, tax, contract, employment, litigation, compliance, IP, privacy/security, and environmental materials, subject to privilege and reasonable confidentiality safeguards. Please identify any access restrictions and propose a process for management Q&A and follow-up requests.
receiver.message_back:
Dear Counsel,

Thank you for the revised draft. The added adjustment, leakage, representation, and indemnification concepts are a helpful basis for discussion, but the material economic and risk-allocation terms remain open. We are not in a position to improve on the Buyer’s USD 30,000,000 proposal without the requested diligence and supporting financial information. Please revise the draft accordingly and provide the specific calculation mechanics and diligence materials described above.

We are available to discuss a practical diligence protocol and a complete set of terms promptly. Nothing in this response waives any Buyer position or makes the draft binding.

Regards,
Bellweather Croft LLP
